title: Editorial Policy

body.value: Digital Truth News Network reports news from Kerala, India and the world in Malayalam and English. Our job is to tell readers what is happening, accurately and fairly, and to explain why it matters.

Our editors decide what we publish. Advertisers, sponsors, owners, political parties and government bodies do not approve, change or stop our news coverage. We follow the Norms of Journalistic Conduct of the Press Council of India and the Code of Ethics for digital news publishers in the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.
Digital Truth News Network is published by Demo Media Private Limited. Demo ownership statement: replace with who owns the publication and how it is funded.
We earn money from advertising, sponsored content (always labelled), reader subscriptions and courses. If a story involves a company or person connected to our owners, we say so in the story.

Accuracy matters more to us than being first.

  • We check facts before we publish, with more than one source for anything disputed or serious.
  • We go to original documents, data and eyewitnesses wherever we can, and say where information comes from.
  • We clearly separate what we know from what is claimed or alleged.
  • Photos, videos and posts from social media are verified (who made them, where and when) before we use them. If we cannot verify something important, we say so.
  • Numbers, names, places and quotes are checked by the reporter and again by the editor.

Sources should be named and their information tested.

  • We name our sources by default, so readers can judge the information for themselves.
  • We grant anonymity only when the information is important, cannot be obtained on the record and the source could face harm or lose their job if named. An editor must know the source's identity and agree.
  • When we use an anonymous source we explain, as far as we can, why they could not be named and how they know what they say.
  • We protect confidential sources and do not reveal them.
  • We do not pay sources for information.

value.text: Fairness, balance and right of reply

body.value:
People we write about deserve to be treated fairly.

  • Before publishing a serious allegation against a person or organisation, we contact them and give them reasonable time to respond. If they do not respond, we say so in the story.
  • We publish a fair summary of the reply, or the reply in full where appropriate, free of charge.
  • We report all relevant sides of a disputed issue and avoid stereotypes. We mention caste, religion, community or other identity only when it is relevant to the story.
  • We do not publish anything meant to promote hatred or enmity between groups.
We make mistakes, and when we do we correct them openly.

value.text: How to ask for a correction

body.value: Use our correction request form, naming the story and what you believe is wrong. We reply as quickly as we can and within the grievance timelines below.

• Errors of fact are corrected in the story, with a dated correction note on the article saying what was wrong and what is right.
  • A major correction (one that changes the meaning of the story) is shown at the top of the article.
  • Small fixes that do not change meaning, such as spelling or grammar, may be made without a note.
  • We never silently change facts. If a story cannot be fixed by a correction, we may take it down and publish a note explaining why.
  • When a story exists in both Malayalam and English, both versions are corrected.

Breaking stories change as we learn more. We add timed live updates to the story and show the time it was last updated. When an update changes the story significantly, it is marked as a major update. Updating with new information is not a correction; correcting an error always gets a correction note.

News reports state facts and the views of the people involved. Opinion, analysis, editorials and reviews are labelled as such, and the author is named. Our reporters keep their personal opinions out of news reports.

• Headlines reflect the story. We do not write misleading or sensational headlines, and allegations in headlines are attributed.
  • We do not alter news photos or video in a way that misleads: no adding, removing or moving people or objects. Cropping and normal colour correction are allowed.
  • Photo illustrations and graphics are labelled.
  • Graphic images of violence, accidents or the dead are used only when essential, with a warning, and with respect for the people shown and their families.
  • Photos and videos from others are used with permission or under a licence, and credited.

Some people need special protection.

  • We respect privacy. We intrude only when there is a clear public interest, and never into grief or shock for its own sake.
  • We never identify a victim of a sexual offence, directly or indirectly: no name, photo, address, relatives, school, workplace or other detail that could lead to them, as the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and the Supreme Court require.
  • We do not identify children who are victims or witnesses of sexual offences (POCSO Act), or children in conflict with the law or in need of care and protection (Juvenile Justice Act). Their photos are not used or are blurred beyond recognition.
  • We report suicide with care: no method, location details, notes or images, no sensational headlines, and every such story carries helpline information, for example Tele-MANAS (14416 or 1-800-891-4416) or the emergency number 112.
  • We do not publish photos or details of people receiving mental health treatment without their consent.

• We report court proceedings fairly and accurately. People are described as accused until a court finds them guilty.
  • We do not publish material that could prejudice a fair trial, and we obey court orders that restrict or postpone reporting.
  • We do not report proceedings held in camera, or the proceedings of sexual-offence trials, without the court's permission.
  • We may criticise judgments on their reasoning, but not attribute motives to judges.
  • During elections we follow the Election Commission's rules on exit polls and the silence period.

• News and advertising are kept strictly apart. Advertisers have no say over our news coverage.
  • Sponsored stories, videos and newsletter messages are always labelled Sponsored and are never made to look like news reports.
  • We do not publish paid news, and our journalists do not sell advertising.
  • Read more on our Advertise With Us page.

• Our journalists tell their editor about any personal, financial or political interest in a story, and do not cover it if the conflict is real.
  • We do not accept gifts, payments or favours that could influence coverage. Small courtesy items, meals at events and review copies may be accepted only where they do not affect what we report, and review products are returned or declared.
  • Paid trips are accepted only when an editor agrees, and the story says who paid.

• We may use AI tools to help with research, transcription, translation drafts, summaries and checking copy. A journalist reviews and verifies everything before it is published, and AI is never treated as a source of facts.
  • We do not publish news written by AI without full review and approval by an editor.
  • We never present AI-generated or AI-altered images, video or audio as real. Any AI illustration is clearly labelled.
  • Where AI materially contributed to a story, for example a translation, we say so.
  • We do not put unpublished material, the identity of sources or readers' personal data into public AI tools.

We publish stories in Malayalam, English or both. When the same story appears in both languages, each version is written or edited separately by a journalist; we do not publish machine translations without review. Both versions are held to the same standards and corrected together.

We welcome news tips, photos and videos from readers through our news tip form. We verify them before using them, credit contributors unless they ask not to be named or naming them could put them at risk, and never publish contributions that break the rules on this page.

• Staff do not post anything on social media that would undermine trust in our impartiality, such as party-political endorsements.
  • They do not break news on personal accounts before it is published by us, and they follow the same standards of accuracy and fairness as on our site.
  • They are courteous with readers and do not share unverified claims.
If you have a complaint about our content (for example its accuracy, fairness, or the privacy of a person in a story), contact our Grievance Officer:

Grievance Officer: Demo Grievance Officer, Grievance Officer
Email: desk@example.com
Address: Demo Building, MG Road, Kochi, Kerala 682001, India

Under the IT Rules, 2021:

  • We acknowledge every complaint within 24 hours.
  • We decide and tell you the outcome within 15 days.
  • If you are not satisfied, you may escalate it as provided in Part III of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.
More on complaints is in our Terms and Conditions.
We review this policy at least once a year and whenever the law changes. The date at the top shows when it was last updated.

seo.description: How Digital Truth News Network reports: accuracy and verification, sources, fairness and right of reply, corrections, privacy, sponsored content, use of AI and grievance redressal.

summary: We check facts before we publish, give people we write about a chance to respond, label opinion and sponsored content clearly, protect victims and children, and correct mistakes openly with a dated note. Advertisers and owners do not decide what we report. If you think we got something wrong, tell us: our Grievance Officer answers within the times set out below.
